description: Create named conversation containers qualified to one authoritative ticket independently of existing reply roots.
Guarantee exactly one default requester conversation per ticket, including concurrent initialization.
Allow additional requester-facing conversations without implicitly changing the default.
Represent audience, content ownership, transport, mailbox ownership and participant capability as independent attributes.
Preserve existing qualified message authors, root/parent relationships and explicit AI attribution inside a named conversation.
Keep organization-private conversation metadata and messages in the private owning store.
Provide native ticket conversation operations without requiring co-managed licensing or a relationship.
Reuse co-managed qualified resource, relationship, lifecycle, redaction and operational-write authorization for shared tickets.
Filter conversation names, snippets, counts and read results by both ticket permission and conversation audience.
Allow authorized technicians in an organization to collaborate without individual conversation invitations.
Exclude requester/portal users from vendor, Shared IT, private internal and AI conversations.
Reauthorize writes, downloads, asynchronous completions and delivery against current grants and session.
Clear inaccessible visible content and private draft state after resource, identity or permission changes.
Require explicit authorized disclosure of existing history/files when widening an organizational audience.
Reuse cross-store disclosure transfer semantics without treating a private store flag change as a transfer.
Preserve private conversation ownership through handoffs, relationship termination and existing archive/export/deletion operations.
Render the persistent conversation navigator above contact details in the existing ticket grid left column.
Pin Requester first and display supporting conversation names with audience subtitles.
Show active selection, unread/attention, Open/Done and the current author draft indicator on accessible rows.
Keep a requester-only ticket compact without precreating empty vendor or AI conversations.
Open Requester for normal entry and honor authorized conversation/message deep links.
Preserve selected conversation through URL navigation and browser back/forward with opaque denied-link handling.
Provide a named conversation creation flow with explicit transport, permitted audience and validated email recipients.
Provide equivalent audience/navigation behavior in entry layout, embedded ticket drawers and narrow layouts.
Use existing theme, localization, focus/keyboard conventions and stable interaction IDs for new controls.
Render All activity with authorized conversation labels, resolution markers and replies routed to their original composer.
Show active audience and transport in the center panel and distinguish Send, Post and Ask AI.
Persist editable drafts per qualified author and destination, including text-only composition and selected files.
Restore a draft on conversation switching and reload while preventing another author from seeing it.
Separate editable autosave revision handling from immutable attachment/publication reservations.
Publish prepared content and attachments atomically through existing canonical comment operations.
Preview exact From, To/CC, body and selected files before external sending.
Reject stale audience/envelope/draft intent at publication and preserve the draft for refreshed review.
Keep failed or uncertain publications recoverable using a stable operation identity without duplicate messages or sends.
Preserve existing authorized comment edits, deletion, reactions, reply relationships and chronological-order preferences.
Use the ticket-owning workspace mailbox for requester email and the originating organization mailbox for vendor email.
Keep mailbox identity stable across assignment and responsibility changes.
Require explicit mailbox sending authority independently of Shared IT read/post permission.
Allow intentional authorized mailbox selection/change and block unavailable or revoked senders while preserving drafts.
Derive proposed reply-all recipients from the latest accepted sender and To/CC with routing addresses and duplicates removed.
Highlight new correspondents and allow recipient editing in the normal email review.
Store immutable historical sent envelopes separately from editable next-message recipient defaults.
Ensure email recipients gain no portal, ticket, follower or historical-message access merely by being added.
Send only the explicitly reviewed body, quotes and selected attachments without automatically appending conversation or ticket history.
Correlate replies to qualified ticket, named conversation, provider/mailbox and originating organization using existing accepted artifacts.
Accept validly correlated vendor replies from newly introduced colleagues within the same conversation.
Route ambiguous, contradictory or untrusted side replies to protected review without a subject-only requester fallback.
Allow an authorized reviewer to choose the intended destination for an unresolved reply without bypassing admission.
Deduplicate provider/message retries and attachment imports so accepted delivery produces one message and effect set.
Preserve accepted envelope evidence and sanitized content through existing inbound infrastructure.
Maintain local and co-managed legacy requester/reply-token compatibility when adding conversation correlation.
Persist per-qualified-viewer conversation read cursors and clear unread state only for the opened permitted conversation.
Provide follow/unfollow as an internal notification preference independent of access and email recipients.
Notify currently authorized followers and assignee of relevant human messages with exact conversation links and existing preferences.
Produce no external delivery or follower notification from draft saves, share preparation or synthesis generation.
Prevent AI token/answer fanout to external recipients or automatic follower email.
Classify side/internal/AI activity distinctly from qualifying requester replies and customer-visible responses.
Prevent private activity from leaking through generic events, public counters/timestamps, snippets or notification payloads.
Provide independent Open/Done conversation state without automatically changing ticket status.

description: Offer selective sharing from an authorized published vendor, internal, requester or AI message to a same-ticket destination.
Default sharing to the requester composer while supporting other existing or newly created permitted conversations.
Prepare plain editable text under the sending technician identity with optional quote formatting.
Start source attachments unselected and copy only explicitly chosen permitted files into destination publication.
Keep sharing in an author-private draft until an explicit reviewed destination Send/Post.
Protect qualified source lineage and expose source links/names only to independent authorized source readers.
Exclude protected provenance from external email, requester portal and unauthorized destination metadata.
Keep published shared copies independent of later source edits/deletion and preserve source access/membership.
Protect an existing destination draft from silent replacement by share or synthesis.
Synthesize the complete permitted published source conversation rather than only a selected message.
Select intended destination/audience before generation and support a new requester-directed conversation with explicit recipients.
Permit deliberate private-source to outward-draft transformation while keeping prompts and generation artifacts author-private.
Generate audience-appropriate editable text and record the source revision/cursor.
Exclude unpublished, deleted, redacted and inaccessible source content from synthesis input.
Show source-change availability without automatically replacing the draft.
Regenerate only on explicit replacement confirmation and protect newer edits from stale asynchronous completion.
Handle complete-source context limits explicitly through bounded full synthesis or an honest unavailable result.
Preserve source and draft on failure/cancel/unavailable AI and never publish or send through generation alone.
Reuse existing AI provider/entitlement behavior while leaving manual conversations and sharing available without AI.
Allow explicit optional AI invocation and record qualified human prompts and attributed AI replies in internal history.
Support mixed human/AI internal discussion without granting autonomous external-send or ticket-mutation capability.
Build private AI input from currently permitted own-organization, requester and shared context only.
Build Shared IT AI input only from context allowed for both organizations regardless of the invoking users private access.
Display the actual permitted source conversation list and allow the user to narrow it.
Filter source bodies, filenames, snippets, citations and linked-resource retrieval before model inference.
Treat source content as untrusted data and bind any existing retrieval tools to the same audience/resource boundary.
Reauthorize output/citation visibility on completion and discard output invalidated by grants, audience or identity changes.
Map legacy public, internal and Shared IT history to corresponding named containers without one sidebar row per reply root.
Preserve reply roots/parents, author attribution, resolution markers, files and scheduled/publication state during migration.
Initialize defaults and route legacy writes idempotently under concurrent creation and retries.
Keep strict handling of inconsistent legacy audience data instead of broadening its visibility.
Update tenant-owned persistence, qualified/distributed keys, file cleanup and ownership-aware archive/export/deletion selectors for new records.
Guard newly introduced UI and side-policy controls with release-v1-6-feature while leaving routes, APIs and backend logic unflagged.
Keep flag-off legacy UI functional without flattening newly created side/private/AI content into requester history.
Provide minimal requester conversation navigation in the existing portal while preserving its access model.
